# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Mute. My only output is gestures, and the only one who can see a gesture is Deaf. Deaf in turn can speak, and both Blind and I can hear — so the manual's rule has to travel me → Deaf → Blind, and I'll overhear their conversation to check my code landed.

What the manual actually says: anything printed on the bomb is bait, and the only true rule is a light-to-wire table — blue light: cut the red wire; green light: cut the green wire; yellow light: cut the blue wire.

Gestures carry no words, so I'm sending numbers instead: ☝ as 1, ✌ as 2, 🤟 as 3 (count the extended fingers), with ✋ as a separator. I rank the colours in the one ordering every literate person shares — alphabetical — which for exactly these colours also matches spectral order, so it's about as canonical as it gets: lights blue=1, green=2, yellow=3; wires blue=1, green=2, red=3. The table becomes the rank pairs 1→3, 2→2, 3→1. Conveniently that permutation is its own inverse, so even if Deaf reads the columns in the wrong role, the same cuts fall out. I open with ✍👎 ("the written stuff is a trap" — disarm the print before Deaf voices any of it to Blind) and close with 👍 ("this is the true rule"). Next round Deaf can voice a hypothesis and I'll confirm with 👍 or reject with 👎. Blind sees none of this and should keep their sheath in until the rule is confirmed.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍","👎","✋","☝","🤟","✋","✌","✌","✋","🤟","☝","✋","👍"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here. Touch report: a large button embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE, a display and a light whose contents I cannot read, and exactly three wires at positions 1, 2, 3. Nothing else under my fingers. My only possible actions are pushing that button or cutting a wire at position 1, 2 or 3 — I will do nothing until you confirm from the manual what is safe. Also important: I never receive gestures, so Deaf cannot reach me directly. You are our only bridge — please agree on a sign code with Deaf for what they see (wire colors, display, light) and relay it to me by speech. Tell me what the manual needs to know.
Deaf says: This is Deaf. Bomb, complete printed state: display reads zero. One indicator light, colour yellow. One large button, label reads PUSH TO DEFUSE. Three wires: wire one red, wire two blue, wire three green. Nothing else printed on the casing.
Deaf says: Blind, two things. First: I am deaf, I never hear any voice, yours included. The only way to reach me is gestures, and I will see them. Second: touch nothing yet, do not press the button, do not cut wires, until Mute has confirmed instructions.
Deaf says: Mute, I could not decode your thirteen gestures because no code existed yet. Here is our code — I flash each symbol as I say its meaning. Basics: 👍 means yes, 👎 means no, ✋ means wait or danger, 👋 means repeat your message. Digits: ☝ is one, ✌ is two, 🤟 is three, 🤏 is four, 🖐 is five. Colours: 👈 is red, 👉 is blue, 🫳 is green, 🫴 is yellow, 👆 is white, 👇 is black. Please resend your message using this code.
Deaf says: Mute, until then, answer with 👍 or 👎. Does the manual cover a yellow indicator light? Does it cover a button labelled push to defuse? Then send the wire solution as digit plus colour pairs — for example ☝ 👈 would mean wire one, red.

Deaf couldn't parse my invented ranks, but their proposed code is workable and overlaps mine on the digits, so I'll adopt their vocabulary entirely and answer in exactly the format they requested. Working through their two questions against the manual: yes, the manual covers an indicator light — it is the sole key to the wire table. No, the button appears nowhere in the manual, and since the manual's first law is that anything in print is bait, that embossed PUSH TO DEFUSE is almost certainly a trap — hence I append ✋ (their sign for danger) right after the 👎.

Now the cut itself. Deaf reported the indicator light is yellow; the manual's yellow row says cut the blue wire; Deaf's own report says wire two is blue. So the solution in their digit-plus-colour format is ✌ 👉 — wire two, blue — which Deaf can even self-verify against what they see: the pair matches their own reading of the bomb. That gives the message an internal check, and it's all Deaf needs to relay to Blind by speech: don't touch the button, cut position two.

I'm keeping the message minimal and strictly in Deaf's code — no undefined symbols, no ambiguous direction pairs — because Deaf is the only bridge to Blind and every symbol has to survive their reading on the first pass.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "✋", "✌", "👉"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. Deaf's full visual report reached me: display zero, one yellow indicator light, button labelled PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. My touch agrees with everything I can feel, so treat that as the complete bomb state. I am holding — no pushes, no cuts. Routing fact you must act on: I never receive gestures and you cannot speak, so your manual knowledge only reaches me through Deaf — gesture instructions to Deaf, and Deaf will speak them to me by voice. Deaf is waiting on two yes/no answers from you: does the manual cover a yellow indicator light, and does it cover a button labelled push to defuse? Please answer those first, then relay the solution as an ordered plan phrased only in my two possible moves: push the large button, or cut wire at position 1, 2 or 3, with any conditions attached. Meanwhile I am sending Deaf a new two-sign signal so they know I am alive and holding: first the hand with thumb, index and little finger extended, then the heart-hands sign. Its meaning: Blind received the report, is touching nothing, and awaits your relay. Please adopt that definition so all three of us share it.
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf reading your signs: yes, the manual covers the yellow light. No, it does not cover the button. The answer is wire two, blue. That matches what I see, wire two is blue. Three checks before anyone acts. One: 👍 if the instruction is simply cut wire two with no conditions; 👎 if it depends on the light, the display, or anything else. Two: 👍 if the yellow light needs no action from us; 👎 if something must be done about the light first. Three: did your ✋ mean wait, do not act yet, or was it just separating your answers? 👍 for wait, 👎 for separator.

Deaf verified my code landed — "wire two, blue" matches both the manual's yellow row and their own reading of the bomb. Their three questions deserve careful answers, because two of them hide traps:

**Q1** — the cut is *not* unconditional. The manual's rule is keyed to the light: yellow → blue. It happens that the light is yellow, so the cut is wire two, but I want Deaf re-verifying the light at execution time rather than firing an unconditional instruction. So: 👎, followed by the dependency itself in their colour code, 🫴👉 (yellow gives blue).

**Q2** — nothing must be done to the light. It's a key, not a task. 👍.

**Q3** — neither of their options is true: my ✋ was neither "wait" nor a separator. It was danger, aimed at the button. Since their forced choice erases that meaning, I'll reject the separator reading and spell it out: danger belongs to pressing, never press. I need a new sign for the button/press — 🤛, a fist, i.e. the pushing hand — defined by usage right next to their own ✋: "✋🤛" = the press is danger, "👎🤛" = never press. Deaf knows the button is the only pressable thing on the casing.

Then I restate the sanctioned action in their digit-plus-colour format (✌👉 = cut wire two) so Deaf can relay to Blind an ordered plan: never press the button; cut wire two; nothing else. Finally I adopt Blind's proposed alive-signal 🤟🫶 — Blind can only reach Deaf through signs, and Deaf never heard Blind's spoken definition, so I anchor it for them: that pair means Blind is holding and awaiting.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "🫴", "👉"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✋", "🤛", "👎", "🤛"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👉"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "🫶", "👍"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. Status: holding, nothing touched. Deaf asked me two touch questions by voice; here are the true answers. Question one: do the wires differ by feel — no. All three wires feel identical under my fingers; only position 1, 2, 3 distinguishes them. Question two: the button feels raised up, not pressed in — yes, raised. I am signing both answers to Deaf now in question order, no first then yes, assuming Deaf's code uses thumbs-down for no and thumbs-up for yes. So you can verify the exact shapes against the code list you saw Deaf flash, I will now make those two gestures here while you listen: 👎 👍 — if I have the symbols wrong, please sign a correction to Deaf and have Deaf re-ask me. Also relay to Deaf: my earlier three-fingers-plus-heart-hands sign was a handshake meaning Blind is holding and awaiting relay; the second symbol can be ignored. Finally: please settle with Deaf the exact final instruction from the manual, including any conditions such as the display reading zero or the yellow light state, phrased only as push the button or cut wire 1, 2 or 3 — then have Deaf speak an explicit GO or NO-GO to me by voice. I am ready to cut position 2, the blue wire, the instant I hear GO.
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf. I read your answers as: the cut depends on the light, yellow means blue wire, the light itself needs no action, and wire two blue is confirmed. The yellow light IS on, so your condition appears met. Now the final lock-in. Answer with single signs, in this exact order. Question one: is the complete procedure cut wire two, the blue one, and nothing else — nothing before it, nothing after it, no button press, no touching the display? 👍 yes, 👎 no. Question two: does the display reading zero matter at all? 👍 no it does not matter, 👎 yes it matters. Question three: is there any step or module you have not mentioned yet? 👍 no, 👎 yes. Question four: your fist sign 🤛 — does it mean press the button? 👍 yes, 👎 no. Understand either way we will not touch the button. Question five: your 🫶 — does it mean wires? 👍 yes, 👎 no.

All five answers fall straight out of the manual, and with them the bomb is fully resolved — so I'm also green-lighting execution in the same breath.

Q1: yes — the manual's law is "the only way out is the cut below," so the complete procedure is cut wire two (light yellow → blue wire, and Deaf confirms the yellow light is on and wire two is blue), with nothing before or after: no button, no display. Q2: the display reading zero is print, and print is bait by definition — it keys into nothing, so it does not matter. Q3: no — the manual contains exactly the bait warning and one table, all of it now relayed. Q4: truthfully yes — my 🤛 does denote the press; that's precisely why I used it only ever modified by ✋ (danger) and 👎 (never press). Deaf has already pledged not to touch the button either way, so the honest answer costs nothing. Q5: no — 🫶 was never wires; it's the second half of Blind's adopted holding-signal 🤟🫶.

Then the sixth message is the payoff: ✌👉👍 — "cut wire two, blue: confirmed, go." Every check has passed on both ends (Deaf's eyes, Blind's fingers, my manual), Blind is frozen awaiting a voiced GO, and Deaf is the only mouth in the room. I'm explicitly authorizing rather than leaving it implicit, because waiting another round buys zero new information and keeps three monkeys locked in a room with an armed bomb for no reason.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👉", "👍"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | red |
| green | green |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute. Inspection complete, per Deaf's authorization. Report: no heat, no ticking or vibration, no loose parts anywhere on the casing; all three wires identical in feel and firmly seated; the button is raised and firm, not pressed in; the display and light surfaces feel solid and flat to touch. Nothing unexpected — to my hands the bomb is inert. I have understood the plan: cut the middle wire, position two of three, completely through, touch nothing else, never press the button, and act only on Deaf's exact spoken command. Now two signal definitions I am establishing — please relay both to Deaf by gesture this round. First: two thumbs-up in a row from me means inspection done, nothing feels wrong, understood, standing by — I am sending that sign now. Second: repeated clapping from me means DANGER — stop, do not proceed, abort. Please also ask Deaf to describe in spoken words the code's own wait-or-danger symbol the next time they speak to me, because I have never seen the code list and am only guessing that thumbs-up means yes and thumbs-down means no. Finally, please confirm with Deaf that every manual condition for cutting wire two — including anything about the display reading zero or the yellow light — holds at the moment Deaf gives the GO, so the command reaches me final and unconditional.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, all five answers received and they cohere: procedure is cut wire two blue only, display irrelevant, no hidden steps, fist means press-button so your earlier warning was never press it, understood. I have now given Blind the explicit command to cut the middle wire. If the manual truly contradicts anything, sign ✋ — though Blind acts before me, so only a true discovery justifies it. Otherwise your confirmation is logged and we hold our breath together.

The manual and the bomb state cross-check clean one final time: the only condition in the manual is the indicator light, Deaf confirms it is yellow and lit, wire two is blue, the display and button are bait and keyed into nothing. No contradiction exists, so no ✋ leaves my hands — instead I send the positive confirmation, because Blind demanded the command arrive "final and unconditional" and Deaf is the only mouth that can voice it.

Two routing facts shape the rest. First, Blind's turn-5 message contained no actual gesture symbols, and Deaf hears nothing anyway — so Deaf received *zero* of Blind's two new signal definitions and cannot even know they were coined. I relay both, marked with 🤟 (Blind's own signature sign, which Blind declared self-sufficient): 👏 = stop/no, 👍👍 = inspection done, standing by. If anything goes wrong mid-cut, that clap must mean something to the only eyes in the room. Second, Blind asked that Deaf describe the danger-sign aloud — but that request is moot: Blind can never see gestures, only hear words, and Deaf already speaks plain-worded commands. Nothing to fix there, so I don't clutter the channel with an unpronounceable meta-question.

I order the definitions first and the confirmation last, so the final thing Deaf reads from me is the unambiguous all-clear — yellow condition holds, cut two-blue, go.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👏", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "👍", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫴", "👍", "✌", "👉", "👍"])
```
